title: `notifications/resources/list_changed`
description: The notification a server sends when the set of available resources changes.
question: Does the framework notice when the resource list changes?
why: Resource sets change far more often than tool sets, because they track real files and records. A stale list means the agent offers context that no longer exists.
usage_note: Not published. Candidate source: count of public MCP servers publishing this. Not estimated, so the panel stays empty until the corpus is scanned.

notes.genkit_js: Genkit (JS) 1.42.0: no handler for `notifications/resources/list_changed` is registered and there is no change hook. Re-listing did not show the change either: `getActiveResources` also calls `resources/templates/list`, the notify fixture does not implement it, and the `-32601` error discards the whole resource list, so both lists came back empty.
notes.mastra: Mastra 2.2.0 against a 2025-11-25 server: `onListChanged('src', fn)` installs the handler, and it fired and the next list showed the change. But the call itself rejects with `subscriptions/listen needs MCP 2026-07-28`, because it also tries to open a 2026-07-28 stream. Code that awaits the registration sees an error for a hook that works.
notes.crewai: CrewAI 1.15.26: `crewai_tools.MCPServerAdapter` exposes only `tools`. It has no resource or prompt API, so there is no list for a notification to refresh.
notes.google_adk: Google ADK 2.11.0: `McpToolset` takes no message handler, so nothing an application registers hears the notification. `list_resources` asks the server on every call, so the next list showed the added resource anyway.
notes.ms_agent_framework: Microsoft Agent Framework 1.21.0: there is no resource API to relist, so a resources list_changed notification reaches `message_handler` and changes nothing the agent can see.
notes.autogen: AutoGen 0.7.5: The workbench registers no message handler, so no hook hears the notification; its `list_resources` asks the server every time, so the next listing shows the change.
notes.strands: Strands Agents 1.59.0: `on_tools_changed` is the only change hook, and it covers tools only. Nothing hears the resources notification, but `list_resources_sync` asks the server every time, so the next listing shows the change.
notes.vercel_ai: Vercel AI SDK (@ai-sdk/mcp 2.0.73): MCPClient registers no notification handler: a server notification reaches only `onUncaughtError`, as an "Unsupported message type" error that does not name the notification. `listResources()` fetches on every call, so the next list shows the added resource.
notes.openai_agents_js: OpenAI Agents SDK (JS) 0.20.0: no handler hears `notifications/resources/list_changed`; the change shows only because the next `listResources` asks the server again.
notes.semantic_kernel: Semantic Kernel 1.45.0: `MCPPluginBase` has no resource list to refresh.
notes.llamaindex: LlamaIndex (llama-index-tools-mcp 0.6.0): `BasicMCPClient` takes no message handler and closes its session after every call (over stdio it also starts a fresh server process per call), so no session is open to hear `notifications/resources/list_changed`, and the next listing did not show the added resource.
notes.google_adk_js: Google ADK (TypeScript) 2.2.1: `MCPToolset` opens a new session for every operation (`getTools`, `listResources`, `readResource`, each tool call) and closes it after; over stdio that is a new server process each time. No session outlives the call that changed the list, and over stdio the added resource dies with its process, so the next `listResources` matched the one before.
notes.agno: Agno 3.1.2: `MCPTools` lists and calls tools only; it has no resource or prompt API, so a resources list_changed notification has nothing to refresh, and no hook hears it.
notes.haystack: Haystack (mcp-haystack 1.5.2): `MCPClient` builds its `ClientSession` with no message handler, and `MCPToolset` has no resource API, so `notifications/resources/list_changed` reaches nothing.
notes.smolagents: smolagents 1.26.0 (mcpadapt 0.1.20): `smolagents.MCPClient` exposes only `get_tools()`. It has no resource or prompt API, so there is no list for a notification to refresh.
notes.dspy: DSPy 3.4.0: DSPy's MCP support is `dspy.Tool.from_mcp_tool`, which converts one tool. It has no resource or prompt API, so resources and prompts stay on the caller's MCP session. No listing means no change to see.
notes.beeai: BeeAI Framework 0.1.85: no resource listing to refresh; BeeAI converts tools only and has no notification hook.
notes.crewai-native: CrewAI 1.15.26, native `crewai.mcp` client (`Agent(mcps=[...])`, not the `crewai_tools.MCPServerAdapter` row): `MCPClient` has `list_tools`, `call_tool`, `list_prompts` and `get_prompt` and no resource API, and `Agent(mcps=...)` turns only the tools into `BaseTool`s, so an agent built on it cannot reach this at all.
notes.google_adk_java: Google ADK (Java) 1.11.0: The adapter registers no `resourcesChangeConsumer` consumer, so nothing tells the agent the list changed. The next `McpToolset.getTools` call (or session `listResources`) lists again and shows the change.
notes.koog: Koog 1.3.0-beta: Koog exposes only tools and registers no list-changed handler. The next `Client.listResources` on the underlying Kotlin SDK `Client` shows the change.
notes.google_adk_go: Google ADK (Go) 2.5.0 (go-sdk 1.8.0): a `ResourceListChangedHandler` on the caller's `*mcp.Client` hears the notification, but mcptoolset lists only tools, so the agent has no resources list to refresh.
